transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I just can’t shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like everything I tried to build after my divorce has collapsed, and I’m just... sitting under it.
Did this heavy, hopeless feeling start after your divorce?
It was after the divorce, yeah, but more specifically it really set in about a month ago, when the financial mess from it started piling up. Since then it’s just been hanging over me.
Do you find that this hopeless feeling comes up mainly when you’re dealing with the financial fallout from the divorce?

It’s not only when I’m dealing with the money stuff. That definitely makes it worse, but the hopeless feeling is kind of just there most of the time. It feels like everything I built after the divorce fell apart, and I’m stuck under it.
Do you feel this hopeless most of the day, even when nothing about the divorce or finances is happening in that moment?
Yes. It’s there most of the day, even when I’m not actively thinking about the divorce or the money. It’s just this heavy, hopeless feeling I can’t seem to get out from under.
Has this heavy, hopeless feeling been present for at least two weeks?
Yes. It’s been about a month now, since the financial mess after the divorce started piling up. It hasn’t really let up.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to that, honestly. I know I’ve been feeling really low, but I can’t say for sure whether I’ve lost interest in the things I usually enjoy.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed or hopeless most of the day for at least two weeks?

Not like this, no. I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling now—like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it. Before this past month, I don’t remember having it this bad for that long.
In the past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m still not sure. I know I feel really down most of the time, but I haven’t really thought about whether things I usually enjoy feel different. I just haven’t been paying attention to it that way.
Have you had trouble sleeping?
Yes. Lately I’m either lying awake staring at the ceiling, thinking over bills and mistakes I made at work, or I wake up way before dawn feeling like I didn’t really sleep at all.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. At work I’ll look at a drainage calculation or a spreadsheet I’ve used for years, and my mind just goes blank. I end up rereading the same numbers over and over and still don’t trust myself to make a decision.
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot?

Yes. I’ve been blaming myself constantly. I keep thinking I’m a terrible engineer, a failed wife, and just a burden. I replay every missed calculation or tense email in my head like it proves I ruin things.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Yes. I’ve had thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. It got intense enough that I scared myself, and I ended up calling the employee assistance program because I didn’t trust where my head was going.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you would expect from the divorce and financial problems alone?

Yes. I mean, the divorce and money problems are awful, but this feels bigger than that. I came in because I can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling—like everything I tried to rebuild after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just stuck underneath it.
